la:noun:far.html:
far, farris, n.
akin with frico, q. v.
,
a sort of grain, spelt, Gr. ζέα, Triticum spelta, Linn.
Prop., the earliest food of the Romans, both roasted and ground into meal, ; ; ; ; sqq.; 18, 30, 72, § 298; ; : adoreum, i. q. far,.— In plur., freq. for corn in general, grain: flava farra, (opp. legumen); ; 219; ; —
Transf., coarse meal, grits, Fragm. XII. Tab. ap. ; ; ; ; ; ; : pium, i. e. mola salsa,; ; cf.: salsa farra,; used in nuptials,; : far caninum,coarse bread for dogs,.

senses: matter of which a thing is composed, i. e. its nature, quality
la:noun:farina.html:
fărīna, ae, f.
far
,
ground corn, meal, flour.
Prop., ; ; ; .—Prov.: facis farinam,i. e. waste, scatter,; .—
Transf., of the dust or powder of other substances resembling meal: folia myrti siccantur in farinam,; cf.: gypsum resolvitur in farinam,: minium tunditur in farinam,; so, cornus cervini,: tofi,: marmoris,: caminorum,.—
Trop., to designate the material of which a thing is composed, i. e. its nature, quality (postAug.): cum fueris nostrae farinae,: Cassius quidam Parmensis quadam epistola ut pistoris nepotem sic taxat Augustum: Materna tibi farina ex crudissimo Ariciae pistrino, etc.,.

la:verb:farcio.html:
farcĭo, farsi, fartum, sometimes farctum (post-class. form farsum, ; ; ;
and farcītum,), 4, v. a.
Gr. φρακ-, φράσσω, to shut in; cf. Lat. frequens; Germ. Berg, Burg
, to stuff, cram, fill full (class.).
Lit.
In gen.: pulvinus perlucidus Melitensi rosa fartus,: medios parietes farcire fractis caementis,: intestinum,: mustelae ventriculus coriandro fartus,: Jovis satelles jecore opimo farta et satiata, etc., Cic. Poët. Tusc. 2, 10, 24; cf.: edaces et se ultra quam capiunt farcientes,.—
In partic., to fatten an animal, = saginare: gallinas et anseres sic farcito,; ; .—
Transf. (rare; not in Cic.).
In gen., to fill, cram with any thing: fartum totum theatrum,filled,: infinitis vectigalibus (rex) erat fartus,; .—
To stuff or cram into: in os farciri pannos imperavit,: totum lignum in gulam,: ischaemon in nares,: hinc farta premitur angulo Ceres omni,i. e. copious, abundant,.—Hence, fartum (farctum), i, n., stuffing, filling, inside: intestina et fartum eorum, cum id animal nullo cibo vivat, etc.,; ; (for which: pulpa fici,): viaticum,a filling for the journey,, acc. to Ritschl.—Comically: fartum vestis, i. q. corpus, (but in , read stragem, v. Ritschl ad h. l.).
